p: Corbett Street sits in east Manchester, close to the SportCity area, and it's handy for the city centre without being in the thick of it.

If your family loves football, the National Football Museum, in the striking glass Urbis building near Victoria Station, is packed with trophies, shirts and interactive games, and it's a great add-on to a day out.

For something completely different, the John Rylands Research Institute and Library on Deansgate is a stunning neo-Gothic building that looks like something out of Harry Potter, and it's free to visit. Kids are often blown away by the reading room.

Castlefield is a lovely corner of the city where canals, old railway viaducts and the remains of a Roman fort sit side by side. It's a great place for a wander, especially on a sunny day, and the Science and Industry Museum is right on the edge of it.
For lots of green space, Heaton Park, in north Manchester, is huge, with play areas, a boating lake and historic Heaton Hall. It's one of the city's big outdoor favourites.
Ancoats and the Northern Quarter, close to the city centre, are packed with independent cafés, bakeries and restaurants, so you'll never be short of somewhere to eat.
Match days at the Etihad can make east Manchester very busy, so it's worth checking the fixtures before setting off. Otherwise, the tram is a handy way to get around without worrying about parking.
With so much going on, a bouncing session here can easily turn into a full weekend in the city.
